Very difficult is the close: ⟦16⟧ (⟦17⟧) ⟦18⟧, while the antistrophe ⟦19⟧ closes: ⟦20⟧, unsuspicious, except that according to the scholia ⟦21⟧ can be added before ⟦22⟧.; the rhythms are thus: ◡ ◡ ◡ —, ◡ ◡ ◡ —, — ◡ — ◡ ◡ —, cf. the Pherecrateans in Str. a. Accordingly, in the strophe one must emend, if these are strophe and antistrophe ⟦23⟧; namely those who repeat the words from ⟦24⟧ after Antistr. ⟦25⟧ as part of this strophe, and those from ⟦26⟧' after ⟦27⟧′ (according to our numbering, according to the other ⟦28⟧′), need not trouble themselves about responsion. Dindorf therefore writes (after Hermann, who however finally chose something else) ⟦29⟧ (⟦30⟧ Arnaldus), also very similar in sound to ⟦31⟧ (⟦32⟧, ⟦33⟧, ⟦34⟧, ⟦35⟧, ⟦36⟧), by which indeed the connection is guaranteed. That then ⟦45⟧ comes from explanation, Hermann already saw; now it says in the one scholion ⟦46⟧, which can indeed also be taken as explanation of ⟦47⟧, but arouses the suspicion that the scholiast to ⟦48⟧ of the text according to his custom supplied ⟦49⟧, in order to be able to construe the accusative. Just so to ⟦50⟧ Ant. ⟦51⟧.. ⟦52⟧, and to 378 ⟦53⟧: ⟦54⟧. On ⟦55⟧ therefore GHermann had already come; with ⟦56⟧. ⟦57⟧ this perhaps cannot be explained directly, but these words can be understood as the remnant of a longer paraphrase. The rhythm is now there: — ◡ — ◡ ◡ —; for precisely in these rhythms trochee and spondee respond without objection, to ⟦58⟧. But now the main thing, the sense.
